transcript:
Agent: Hello, good morning! Am I speaking with Rajesh Mehta?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is calling?

Agent: Rajesh, this is Priya from Finserve Collections. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account with us. Account number ending in 4827. Do you have a few minutes to talk?

Customer: Haan, okay, but I'm quite busy right now. What is this about?

Agent: Sir, I'm calling because your account shows an outstanding balance of rupees 1,87,450, and the payment is overdue by 45 days now. Your last EMI was due on the 15th of last month. Can you help me understand what happened?

Customer: <interruption> Yes, yes, I know about this. Look, the thing is... I lost my job, yaar. Three weeks ago my company shut down operations. They just told everyone to leave without proper notice, without severance package, nothing. So right now I don't have any income coming in.

Agent: Oh, I see. I'm sorry to hear that, Rajesh. That must be very stressful. When exactly did this happen?

Customer: It was around the 20th of last month. The company was having financial problems for a while, but we didn't think they would just close down like this. Now I'm sitting at home, and I have no money coming in. My wife is asking me every day, "What are we going to do?" I have EMIs on this loan, my home loan, and my credit card bills also pending.

Agent: I understand. This is a difficult situation. So you're currently unemployed and looking for work, is that correct?

Customer: Yes, correct. I've been sending out resumes, but the job market is not good right now, especially in my field. It takes time to find something, no? Meanwhile, how am I supposed to pay all these bills? <interruption> Sorry, I'm just... I'm very stressed about this whole thing.

Agent: No, no, I completely understand, Rajesh. This is not your fault. Let me ask you this — do you have any savings or any other source of income that we can work with right now?

Customer: Some savings, yes, but not much. Maybe 50,000 rupees in my account. But that's for household expenses, for groceries, electricity bill, rent payment. My landlord is also waiting for rent. If I give that to you, my family will have nothing to eat.

Agent: I see. So you're in a very tight situation. Tell me, when do you think you might find another job? Do you have any interviews lined up or any prospects?

Customer: I have been shortlisted for two positions, but the process is slow, yaar. One company will give feedback in 2 weeks, maybe 3 weeks. Another one might take even longer. I'm also trying to do some freelance work on the side, but it's not bringing in enough money to cover all my expenses.

Agent: Okay, so there's some hope with these interviews. That's good. Now, Rajesh, I want to help you here. We cannot ignore the outstanding amount, but we also understand that you're going through a hardship. I need to assess your situation properly before I can offer you any restructuring or relief options.

Customer: What kind of options? Can you reduce the EMI or something? Give me some time?

Agent: Those are possibilities, yes. But first, I need some information. Can you tell me — when you were working, what was your monthly salary?

Customer: Around 85,000 rupees per month. That was my take-home salary.

Agent: And your current monthly obligations — the loan EMI, home loan EMI, credit card bills — how much in total?

Customer: The EMI on this personal loan is 18,500 rupees. Home loan is around 22,000. Credit card payments, sometimes 8,000, sometimes more. So roughly 48,000 to 50,000 rupees every month. That was manageable when I had my salary, but now... <interruption> now I have nothing.

Agent: I understand. So your total obligations were roughly 48 to 50 percent of your income, which was manageable, but now with no income, it's impossible. That's a genuine hardship situation.

Customer: Exactly. And I'm not refusing to pay, okay? I'm not trying to run away from my responsibility. But I literally don't have the money right now. What am I supposed to do?

Agent: I hear you, Rajesh. You're not refusing, you're in a temporary difficult situation due to job loss. That's different. Now, I'm going to escalate your case to my supervisor. Based on what you've told me, you may be eligible for a temporary moratorium — that means we pause your EMI for maybe 2 to 3 months while you find employment. Once you get a job, we can resume the EMI, maybe with a revised repayment schedule.

Customer: Really? Can you do that?

Agent: I can request it. But I need you to commit to a few things. First, you need to provide documentation of your job loss — a termination letter or separation letter from your company. Second, you need to update us as soon as you secure a new job. And third, you need to keep in touch with us during this moratorium period.

Customer: Yes, I can do that. I have the separation letter. I can send it to you. But how long will this take? Will you still call me every day?

Agent: No, no, once we put you on moratorium, the collection calls will pause. We'll only follow up once a month to check your status. And we'll send you a formal letter confirming the moratorium terms. It usually takes 3 to 5 working days for approval.

Customer: Okay, that sounds better. At least I can breathe a little bit. But can I ask — even after I get a job, will my EMI go back to the same 18,500 rupees, or will it increase because of the interest that's accumulating now?

Agent: That's a valid question. The moratorium will freeze the interest accrual on the principal, but there may be some minor late fees that have already been applied. We'll provide you a complete revised statement once the moratorium is approved. But the idea is not to burden you further — we want to help you get back on your feet.

Customer: Okay. Thank you for this. I was really worried that you would just threaten me or be rude. I'm glad you're listening.

Agent: That's what we're here for, Rajesh. I'm going to document this call now. I'll create a formal request for moratorium and escalate it to my supervisor. You should receive a call from our supervisor or an email within 3 working days with the approval and the moratorium letter. In the meantime, can you please send that separation letter to this email address: collections-hardship@finserve.com?

Customer: Yes, I can do that today itself. Is there anything else I need to send?

Agent: Just the separation letter is fine for now. And Rajesh, one more thing — keep applying for jobs, stay positive. These things take time, but the situation will improve. We're here to support you during this difficult period.

Customer: Thank you. I really appreciate this. I'll send the letter today.

Agent: Perfect. Thank you for cooperating, Rajesh. We'll be in touch soon. Have a good day.

Customer: You too. Thank you again.
L3: Hardship – Job Loss / Income Disruption|Disputes Outstanding Amount – Claims Less Owed|Other Lender EMI – Mentioned as Competing Priority|Identity Confirmed – Borrower Verified on Call|Salary Credit – Expected Before Payment Date|Commitment Conditional – Subject to External Factor|Vulnerability Detected – Distress Signal on Call

Customer: Nahi, 13,000 nahi. Aur interest bhi kam karo. Dekho, agar mujhe 12,000 hi de sakta hoon monthly, toh 4 mahine mein settlement hona chahiye. Matlab 45,000 abhi, 12,000 x 4 = 48,000. Total 93,000. Toh interest toh sirf 8,000 ka banega. Yeh fair hai na?

Agent: <interruption> Sir, aapka calculation... wait. Toh aap keh rahe ho — 45,000 on 5th December, phir 12,000 per month for 4 months?

Customer: Haan, bilkul. Aur penalty waived. Toh interest sirf 8,000 ka banega, jo acceptable hai.

Customer: Haan bhaiya, 5th December ko 45,000, phir har mahine 12,000. Salary aa jaayegi toh kar dunga. Lekin agar December mein salary delay ho gaya, toh kya hota hai?

Agent: Agar salary delay ho, toh aap hume immediately inform kar dena. Lekin commitment toh yeh hai na — 45,000 on 5th December. Aur sir, aapka address confirm karte hain — aap abhi bhi Sector 12, Noida mein ho na?

Customer: Haan, wohi address hai. Lekin wait, aapne kaha na penalty waived? Toh total outstanding sirf kitna banega?

Agent: Sir, total outstanding 85,000 tha. Minus penalty 8,000. Toh ab 77,000 banega. Aur interest 9% ke hisaab se lagega. Toh aapka total settlement amount approximately 85,000 hi rahega, lekin penalty waived. Aap 45,000 + (12,000 x 4) = 93,000 denge, toh interest thoda kam hoga.

Customer: Toh settlement amount 85,000 hi hai? Theek hai, main 45,000 December ko de dunga, phir har mahine 12,000. Aur mujhe confirmation chahiye email par.

Agent: Bilkul sir. Hum aapko settlement letter bhej denge, jisme sab kuch likha hoga. Aapka contact number confirm hai na — 98765-43210?

Customer: Haan, wahi number hai. Aur email — rajesh.kumar1985@gmail.com. Confirmation zaroor bhej dena.

Agent: Bilkul sir. Toh aapka settlement confirm ho gaya. 45,000 on 5th December, phir 12,000 per month for 4 months. Penalty waived. Aur hum aapko settlement letter email kar denge. Kya aapko aur kuch chahiye?

Customer: Nahi bhaiya, bas yeh confirm kar do ki agar main 5th ko payment kar du, toh aapne mujhe dobara call nahi karna. Aur collection activity band ho jaayegi?

Agent: Haan sir, bilkul. Agar aap settlement ke according payment kar do, toh collection calls band ho jaayenge. Lekin agar kisi mahine payment miss ho gaye, toh hum call kar denge. Toh commitment confirm hai na?

Customer: Haan, commitment confirm hai. 45,000 on 5th December, phir 12,000 per month. Chalo, aur baat mat karo.

Customer: I do have another account, but that is a joint account with my wife. I cannot withdraw or transfer without her signature. And she is not in the city right now. She will be back next week.

Agent: I completely understand your frustration, Rajesh. You want to pay, the funds are available, but the bank's compliance hold is preventing you from doing so. This is not a refusal on your part, and I appreciate your honesty about the situation. Let me note this down in your account.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Mr. Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya from Infinity Finance Collections. I'm calling regarding your loan account ending in 4782. Do you have a moment to speak?

Customer: Yes, yes, I have some time. But listen, I need to tell you something — I already received a call last week about this, and I'm confused about the amount they told me.

Agent: No problem, Rajesh. I'm here to help clarify. What is the confusion regarding the amount?

Customer: See, my outstanding balance shown in your system is Rs. 1,47,000 rupees, but according to my own calculation and my bank statements, I should owe only around Rs. 1,05,000. You people have added extra charges — interest, some processing fee, I don't know what all. When I took the loan, it was for Rs. 1 lakh, and I've been paying regularly every month.

Agent: I understand your concern, Rajesh. Let me pull up your account statement here. <pause> Okay, so I can see the account shows an outstanding of Rs. 1,47,250. This includes your principal amount remaining, accrued interest, and yes, there is a late fee that was applied after you missed a payment in July. Can you tell me which of these components you're disputing?

Customer: That July payment — I did not miss that. I paid it on time. I have the receipt, actually I have the bank confirmation. The payment was made on July 8th, but your system is still showing it as missed. That's the problem. Because of that wrong marking, you've added a penalty of Rs. 8,000 that I shouldn't have to pay.

Agent: Okay, that's helpful to know. Let me check our payment records for July 8th. <interruption> Sorry, can you give me the reference number from your bank confirmation?

Customer: Yes, the NEFT reference is 2024070800456789. I transferred it directly to your account. I'm looking at the statement right now.

Agent: Thank you. Let me verify this in our system. <pause> Hmm, I'm not seeing this credit reflected in our July records. It's possible there was a processing delay or the payment was received after our cut-off time. But I need to escalate this to verify. This is definitely something we need to look into because if the payment did come through on July 8th, then the penalty should not have been applied.

Customer: Exactly! And because of this wrong penalty, the entire outstanding amount has become inflated. If you remove the Rs. 8,000 penalty and recalculate, I think I will owe closer to Rs. 1,39,000, not Rs. 1,47,000. But even that — I'm not sure about the interest component. Can you send me the full ledger showing how the interest was calculated month by month? Because the interest rate you're charging seems higher than what was mentioned in my loan agreement.

Agent: That's a fair request, Rajesh. I can definitely arrange for a detailed ledger to be sent to you. However, let me confirm — are you disputing the interest rate itself, or the amount of interest that's been charged?

Customer: Both, actually. The agreement said the rate would be 14 percent per annum, but when I calculated backwards from your numbers, it looks like you're charging closer to 16 percent. And then there's also a processing fee of Rs. 2,500 that I see on the statement. I don't remember agreeing to pay that separately. All these things add up, and that's why the number is so different from what I calculated.

Agent: I see. So you're raising three points — the missed July payment that resulted in the penalty, the interest rate discrepancy, and the processing fee that you don't recall authorizing. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, exactly. I want to settle this, but I need clarity on these charges first. If you can correct the records and send me a proper statement, then I can commit to a payment. But right now, I'm not going to pay Rs. 1,47,000 for something I don't owe.

Agent: Rajesh, I completely understand your position. What I'll do is this — I will escalate your July payment reference to our back-office team to verify if that NEFT actually cleared. I'll also request a recalculated statement with a month-by-month interest breakup and a clarification on the processing fee. Once I have verified all of this, I'll call you back within 48 hours with a corrected statement. Does that work for you?

Customer: Yes, that sounds good. But can you also check if there was any overpayment? Because if you've been charging me wrong interest, maybe I've already paid more than I should have, and you owe me a refund.

Agent: That's a good point. Once we verify all the charges, we'll definitely check for any overpayment and flag it for refund if applicable. I'm making a note here — we need to verify the July 8th NEFT payment, recalculate interest at the correct rate, clarify the processing fee, and check for overpayment. I'll personally follow up with you within two days.

Customer: Okay, thank you. And please, when you call back, have the correct information ready. I don't want to keep going back and forth on this.

Agent: Absolutely, Rajesh. I appreciate your patience, and I assure you we'll get this sorted. I'm noting your contact number as 98765-43210 — is that still the best number to reach you?

Customer: Yes, that's fine. Call me after 5 PM, preferably in the evening.

Agent: Perfect. I'll follow up by 6 PM two days from now. Thank you for your time, Rajesh, and sorry for the inconvenience.

Customer: Okay, thanks.

Customer: Look, I know about the EMI. I've been meaning to call you people myself actually. This whole thing is not fair, yaar. The amount you're showing me is completely wrong.

Agent: I appreciate you sharing that, Rajesh. Let me note down the UPI reference you mentioned. However, I will need to verify that payment against our records. In the meantime, the remaining balance of Rs. 5,600 from your original EMI plus the applicable charges—

Customer: <interruption> Applicable charges? What applicable charges? I already told you I paid Rs. 15,000. You people are just trying to squeeze more money out of me. And frankly, I've had enough of this. I've been getting calls from your team three times a day, sometimes at 8 in the morning, sometimes at 9 at night. Is this even legal?

Regarding the charges, the late fee is standard when a payment is not made within the due date. But let's focus on resolving this. Once we verify your payment of Rs. 15,000, we can adjust the account accordingly. When can you make the remaining payment?

My advocate has already advised me that your collection practices may violate consumer protection laws, and frankly, the amount you're claiming is incorrect. So from now on, you need to communicate only through my legal representative. I'm not taking any more calls from your team directly.

Agent: Rajesh, I understand you're frustrated, but—

Customer: <interruption> Frustrated? This is beyond frustration. My lawyer will be sending you a formal notice. Do not call me again. Any further communication regarding this loan should go through my legal counsel. I have their contact details ready, and trust me, they will be in touch with you. I'm also considering filing a complaint with the RBI about your collection practices. This call itself is evidence of harassment. Now, do you understand what I'm saying?

Agent: Yes, Rajesh, I understand. I will make a note that you have legal representation and—

Customer: Good. My lawyer is Advocate Sharma at Sharma & Associates. That's the only contact you should be using. Goodbye.

Agent: Thank you for—

Customer: <interruption> I said goodbye.

Agent: Absolutely. I'm putting a note on your file that you are facing a medical hardship with your father's hospitalization. No calls will be made to you for the next fifteen days. transcript:
Agent: Hello, is this Anjali Desai?

Customer: Yes, speaking. Who is this?

Agent: Hi Anjali, this is Vikram calling from Finserve Collections. I'm reaching out about your loan account, account number ending in 5634. Your monthly EMI of rupees 22,000 was due on the 10th. We haven't received payment yet. Are you there?

Customer: Haan, yes, I'm here. Listen, I... I know the payment is late. I know that. But the thing is, you see, my husband, he handles all the money now. Like, all of it. My salary used to come into my account, but he said it's better if everything comes to his account now. Better for tax purposes, he said. And now I don't have access to anything without asking him first. He's very... he's very particular about how money is spent.

Agent: I see. So you're unable to access funds directly to make the payment yourself?

Customer: Not just unable, Vikram. I don't have any money in my name. None. He took my ATM card six months ago. He said I don't need it. And when I ask him about these bills, these EMIs, he gets so angry. Like, really angry. He shouted at me yesterday for two hours because I mentioned we need to pay the electricity bill. Two hours, Vikram. And then he didn't speak to me for the rest of the day.

Agent: Anjali, I'm sorry to hear that. Has he said whether he'll pay this EMI? Have you asked him yet?

Customer: <interruption> No, I haven't asked him. I'm... I'm scared to ask. Last time I mentioned a bill, he said it was my fault for taking the loan in the first place. He said I'm irresponsible with money. But he agreed to the loan! We both did! Now he acts like I did it behind his back. And I never know what mood he'll be in. One day he's fine, the next day he's angry about something small. I can't predict it anymore.

Agent: <pause> Anjali, let me ask you something. Are you safe at home? Is everything okay?

Customer: <long pause> I don't... I don't want to get into all that. I just need time. Can you call me back in a few weeks? Maybe by then I can figure something out. Maybe he'll be in a better mood or something.

Agent: Of course. I hear you. Before we wrap up though — is there any way you could make even a small payment yourself? From savings, or—

Customer: No, Vikram. I have nothing. I stopped working last year. He asked me to. He said he didn't want me going to the office every day. And now I have no income, no savings, nothing. Everything depends on him. I'm completely dependent.

Agent: <pause> Okay, Anjali. I want you to listen to me carefully. I'm going to pause the normal collection process right now. What I'm doing is flagging your account for specialist handling. You don't need to make any decisions today, and you don't need to worry about the usual follow-ups. We're going to assign you to a trained agent who understands situations like yours — someone who can talk to you without pressure, at whatever pace you need.

Customer: <quietly> Really? You're... you're just going to stop?

Agent: Yes. We're going to stop the standard process. Your account is being marked as needing specialist care. And Anjali, if you ever need to talk to someone, or if you need support or resources, there are organisations that help people in situations like yours. I'll make a note of that too.

Customer: Thank you. I... I appreciate that more than you know. I just didn't know what to do.

Agent: You did the right thing by being honest with me. Take care of yourself, okay? We'll be in touch in a couple of weeks with a different approach. Is there anything else you want to tell me today?

Customer: No, I think that's all. Thank you, Vikram.

Agent: Thank you, Anjali. Look after yourself.

Customer: Haan, yes, speaking. But I'm in the middle of something, yaar. What is this about?

Agent: Sir, I'm calling because your account is currently overdue. Our records show you owe 2,14,600 rupees, and your last payment was back in July. We need to discuss this urgently.

Customer: <interruption> Wait, wait, wait. 2,14,600? That's not right, no? I paid — I made a payment just last month. On August 10th I went to the Bandra branch and deposited 45,000 rupees. Then before that also I paid through UPI. So how can the amount be so much, yaar?

Agent: Okay sir, I understand. Let me check your payment history. Which UPI payment are you referring to?

Customer: It was July 30th, 25,000 rupees. I have the transaction ID and everything. So together that is 70,000 rupees I paid last month only. Your system is not updated or something, no?

Agent: Let me verify sir. I can see the July 30th UPI payment of 25,000 rupees is showing in our system. But the August 10th branch deposit of 45,000 — I'm not seeing that yet. It's possible the bank is still processing it. But based on the confirmed UPI payment, your balance should be lower than what I initially stated.

Customer: This is the problem, no? The teller gave me a receipt. Receipt number BR-89234-AUG. I have it right here. How can it not be in the system? And even if that one is delayed, at least the 25,000 should be adjusted, so you are showing me wrong amount, yaar.

Agent: You're absolutely correct sir, and I apologize. Based on the UPI payment of 25,000 that is confirmed, your outstanding should be approximately 1,89,600, not 2,14,600. That's my mistake in the initial figure.

Customer: Okay so you agree your number was wrong. But what about the 45,000 I deposited? When will that show up, haan? And also, I want to know — why am I being charged extra? I see in the SMS they sent me there is a processing fee of 700 rupees added to my EMI, and also a penalty of 500 rupees. The original EMI was 28,500 rupees. So I paid 29,200 rupees. I never agreed to these extra charges, no?

Agent: Sir, those are valid questions. Can you tell me — the 700 rupees processing fee, was that charged when you made a late payment? And the 500 rupees penalty — do you know when that was applied?

Customer: I don't know exactly when, but I just know I paid more than the EMI I agreed to. That is not fair, no? And I want a proper statement showing what I actually owe without these charges. Because if my EMI is 28,500, then I should pay 28,500 only, not 29,200. These extra charges — I don't agree with them.

Agent: Sir, I completely understand your frustration. So to be clear, you are disputing three things — the 45,000 rupees branch deposit that hasn't been reflected, the 700 rupees processing fee, and the 500 rupees penalty charge. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, exactly that. I want to know what I actually owe. Because once that 45,000 is credited, and if you remove these charges, my actual balance should be much lower than what you are saying now. Send me a detailed statement showing everything — all charges, all payments, everything. Then we can talk properly.

Agent: Sir, I will absolutely prepare a detailed account statement and ledger showing the breakup of all charges and all your payments. I'll also personally follow up with our back-office team regarding the status of your 45,000 rupees branch deposit. Can I have your email address to send this statement?

Customer: It's arun.patel.1985@gmail.com. But once you send me this, you need to verify these charges properly, yaar. Because I don't think I should be paying for charges I didn't agree to in the first place.

Agent: Sir, I will send you the complete statement within 24 hours. Once you review it and confirm the details, we can escalate any disputed charges to my supervisor for verification against your original loan agreement. The processing fee and penalty may be applicable under the terms, but I understand your concern and we will verify it properly. Can I also confirm your current contact number?

Customer: It's 9876543210. And please, send that statement quickly. I don't want to pay extra charges that I didn't consent to. Once we verify everything, then we can decide what I actually owe and how I will pay, no?

Agent: Absolutely sir, I'm noting all of this down right now. I will send the statement by tomorrow morning, and I will call you on the 15th to discuss the verified amounts. By that time the branch deposit should also show up. Does that timeline work for you?

Customer: Yes, that's fine. But make sure you send it, yaar. And check properly about the 45,000 rupees deposit with the bank. I have the receipt, so it should be there.

Agent: Understood sir. I will personally ensure the statement is sent and I will also track the branch deposit with the bank. Thank you for your patience, Arun. We'll resolve this properly once you've reviewed the statement.

Customer: Okay, thank you. Just make sure you follow up, no?

Agent: Absolutely sir. We'll be in touch by the 15th.

transcript:
Agent: Namaste, am I speaking with Rajesh Sharma?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Amit from Reliance Finance. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4827. Do you have a few minutes to talk?

Customer: <interruption> Arre, not again. I got a call yesterday also. What is it now? The payment, haan? Look, I know I'm late, but I'm handling it.

Agent: Yes, I understand. I can see your account is about 45 days overdue with an outstanding amount of 1,84,500 rupees. We want to help you catch up. Can we discuss your situation?

Customer: <interruption> Dekho, the amount you're showing is wrong. I paid 50,000 rupees last month through NEFT. Your system shows 1,84,500 but it should be less than 1,35,000. You people never update properly.

Agent: I see your concern, Rajesh. Let me verify that payment for you. Can you share the NEFT reference number?

Customer: Reference is HDFC1207NEF4521. I have the receipt also. But anyway, right now I don't have the full amount. My salary comes on the 15th of next month. After that, I can pay.

Agent: Thank you for that reference. I will verify this payment immediately. So after your salary comes on the 15th, can you commit to paying the full outstanding amount?

Customer: Haan, 15th ko salary aayega, phir I will pay. But before that, I need this amount issue sorted first, yaar. I don't want to pay twice. Also, my wife is out of station right now and she's a co-applicant on this loan. I need to speak with her also before I commit to any large payment.

Agent: I completely understand. Let me note down that you're expecting to pay after the 15th once your salary arrives. We will also verify your NEFT payment and update the amount. Regarding your wife, is she available to speak later today?

Customer: No, no, she comes back only on the 20th. So maybe you call me after that, or after the 15th when I have the salary. But please, not in the morning, yaar. I sleep late. Call me after 5 PM, in the evening. That is better for me.

Agent: Perfectly fine, Rajesh. So I'm noting down that we should call you back on or after the 15th of next month, after 5 PM in the evening. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, yes, that is correct. And make sure you have sorted out this amount issue by then. I'm not paying 1,84,500 when I already paid 50,000. That is my condition.

Agent: Absolutely. I will personally ensure that your NEFT payment is verified and the amount is corrected in our system. We will call you back after the 15th, between 5 PM and 7 PM. How does that sound?

Customer: Good. And one more thing — please don't call before that date. I have told you my situation. I will pay after salary, but I need time. And I need the amount corrected first.

Agent: Understood completely, Rajesh. No calls before the 15th. We will verify everything and reach out to you in the evening after the 15th. Thank you for your time and cooperation.

Customer: Okay, thank you. Bye.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh. But I am very busy right now. What is this call regarding?

Agent: Namaste, Mr. Kumar. My name is Priya from ICICI Fintech Collections. I am calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4827. Your EMI payment of rupees 8,500 was due on the 15th of this month, and we have not yet received it. Can we discuss your payment status?

Customer: Haan, I know about the EMI. Look, I have been meaning to call you actually. The thing is, I have submitted all my documents to my HR department for a salary revision letter. I got promoted three months back, and the bank asked me to provide an updated income certificate before I can... before I can make any large payment commitment.

Agent: I see. That sounds like positive news regarding your promotion, Mr. Kumar. So you are waiting for this income certificate from your employer?

Customer: Yes, exactly. My HR is very slow, yaar. They said they will issue the letter by next Thursday, 22nd of this month. Once I have that, I can approach my bank and sort out my account situation. Right now, I don't want to make a promise I cannot keep because of some documentation issue.

Agent: That makes complete sense. Can I ask — do you have any idea about the timeframe after you receive the letter? Will you be able to submit it to us immediately, or is there any further processing needed?

Customer: (<interruption>) Once I get the letter, I will... I will forward it to you the same day via email. Then your team can verify it and... and we can sit down and plan the repayment properly. Maybe a restructuring, maybe increased EMI, I don't know yet. But I need that letter first.

Agent: Understood, Mr. Kumar. So the income certificate is critical before you can commit to any repayment plan or restructure. And you are expecting it by the 22nd?

Customer: Yes, 22nd. That is what HR told me. But sometimes they are late, so I am a bit worried. If it gets delayed, I will call you immediately. I promise I will not disappear.

Agent: Thank you for that assurance. I will make a note that we are awaiting your updated income certificate from your employer, expected by the 22nd of this month. Once you receive it, please email it to our collections team at the email address I am about to share, or you can call me directly. Can I share that email?

Customer: Yes, go ahead.

Agent: The email is collections-follow-up@icicifintech.com. Please use the subject line "Loan Account 4827 - Income Certificate" so we can track it properly. Is there anything else blocking your payment right now, or is it purely the documentation?

Customer: No, the documentation is the main thing. Once I have that letter, I have the funds to pay. The promotion has increased my salary, so I am in a better position than before. I just need to prove it to the bank.

Agent: That is excellent news, and I am very glad to hear your financial situation has improved. I will schedule a follow-up call for the 23rd of this month to check on the status of the income certificate. Does that work for you?

Customer: Yes, 23rd is fine. Call me after 6 PM if possible, because I am in office meetings most of the day.

Agent: Perfect. I have noted that down — follow-up call on the 23rd after 6 PM. Mr. Kumar, just to confirm: once you provide the income certificate, we will need a few days to verify it internally. But you understand that your account is currently overdue by one EMI, so as soon as we receive and verify the certificate, we would like you to make a payment or enter into a formal restructure agreement. Is that clear?

Customer: Yes, I understand. I will not delay once I have the documents. This is my first time defaulting, and I want to get this sorted quickly.

Agent: I appreciate your cooperation, Mr. Kumar. Your account reflects that this is indeed the first missed payment, and we value your proactive communication. We will be in touch on the 23rd. Thank you for your time.

Customer: Thank you. Goodbye.

Agent: Goodbye, Mr. Kumar. Have a good day.
L3: Salary Credit – Expected Before Payment Date

transcript:
Agent: Namaste, main Rajesh bolu, Finquest Credit se bol raha hoon. Kya main Shri Vikram Sharma se baat kar sakta hoon?

Customer: Haan haan, ek minute. Actually, main Vikram ke ghar se bol raha hoon. Vikram yahan nahi hain abhi.

Agent: Okay, to aap kaun ho? Aap Vikram ke ghar se kyu baat kar rahe ho?

Customer: Main unke bete hoon, Arjun. Papa ke liye call aa raha hai kya? Unpaid EMI ke baare mein?

Agent: Haan Arjun, bilkul. Vikram Sharma ke account mein 47,000 rupees outstanding hain. Due date tha 15th November. Ab hum collection call kar rahe hain. Kya aap apne father ko available kar sakte ho?

Customer: <interruption> Bhai, yeh... yeh sab complicated hai. Ek minute, main aapko batata hoon. Papa approximately teen mahine pehle... unhe ek bahut bada stroke aaya tha. Abhi unhe baat karna bahut difficult hai. Unka left side completely paralyzed ho gaya.

Agent: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Vikram ko medical condition hai to? Kya unhe hospital mein admit kiya gaya tha?

Customer: Haan, Apollo mein tha do mahine tak. Ab ghar par hain par unhe speech therapy chal rahi hai aur sab. Wo abhi baat kar nahi sakte properly. Aur finances... sab mera handle karna pad raha hai ab. Mummy bhi weak ho gai hain stress se.

Agent: Samjha, samjha. This is really difficult situation. Arjun, tum apne father ke account ka access hai? Loan ke bare mein tum kuch samjhte ho?

Customer: Haan, maine sab dekha. Papa ne kuch saal pehle ye personal loan li thi. 4 lakh ka loan tha, monthly EMI 47,000 rupees. Par last three-four mahine se hum payment nahi kar paaye. Hospital bills, medicines, physiotherapy... sab kuch bahut expensive ho gaya. Aur Papa ke salary to stop ho gai ab.

Agent: Okay, I understand. So Vikram's income has stopped due to his medical condition. Arjun, are you employed? Can you help with the repayment?

Customer: Main hoon, par main bhi startup mein kaam karta hoon. Salary fixed nahi hai. Aur mera apna chhota sa loan bhi hai. <interruption> Yaar, Papa ke liye sab kuch medical bills mein jaa raha hai. We are struggling honestly.

Agent: I can see that. Arjun, mujhe confirm karna padega — Vikram abhi call mein aa sakte hain? Even if speech difficult hai, main unse bas confirm karna chahta hoon ki account unka hi hai.

Customer: Nahi nahi, wo bilkul nahi bol sakte. Doctor ne kaha hai emotional stress avoid karna padega unhe. Agar main unhe phone hold karun to unhe anxiety attack aa jayega. Wo to bass bed par baithe hain, TV dekh rahe hain.

Agent: Understood. Arjun, this is a very sensitive situation. Hospital reports hai aapke paas? Doctor's certificate ya kuch?

Customer: Haan, sab discharge papers hai. CT scan, everything documented hai. Agar aapko chahiye to main bhej dunga. Par ek cheez samjhiye — Papa ko abhi recovery mein hain. Unhe kaise EMI pay karte? Unka to income zero hai abhi.

Agent: <interruption> Bilkul samjha. Arjun, hum yeh understand kar rahe hain ki Vikram incapacitated hain medically. This changes everything for us. Normally hum borrower se directly contact karte hain, but agar borrower able nahi hai to...

Customer: Haan, that's why I'm calling you. Main unke behalf mein baat karna chahta tha, par aap ne bhi kaha na ki verification chahiye. Papa ke paas to documentation sab hai stroke ka. Kya yeh enough nahi hai?

Agent: Haan, documentation help karega. Arjun, mujhe apna supervisor se baat karni padegi. This case requires special handling. Vikram's account ko hum immediately suspend kar denge collections activity se. Hum bereavement aur incapacity team ko escalate karenge.

Customer: Bereavement? Papa to abhi zinda hain! Woh to recover kar rahe hain.

Agent: No no, I apologize — I meant incapacity team, not bereavement. Incapacity means when borrower physically unable hai. Hum Vikram ko medical relief options provide kar sakte hain. Moratorium, payment holiday, restructure — sab possible hai.

Customer: Okay, that's good. Kab tak ye process chalega?

Agent: Arjun, within three business days hum aapko call karenge specialist team se. Please ensure hospital discharge summary aur doctor's report ready ho. Iske saath identity aur address proof bhi chahiye hoga Vikram ka.

Customer: Sab kuch arrange kar dunga. Aur haan, Papa ke account pe koi aur calls nahi aayenge na ab?

Agent: No, bilkul nahi. Account ko do-not-contact flag laga denge. Sirf specialist team se contact hoga, aur wo bhi very carefully. Arjun, aapka mobile number kya hai? Hum usi par contact karenge.

Customer: 98765-43210. Aur ek ek minute, Papa ke salary account ka statement bhi bhej dunga. Dikhana chahta hoon ki income zero hai.

Agent: Perfect. Thank you for the cooperation, Arjun. Yeh very compassionate approach hai aapka. Hum Vikram ke case ko priority denge. Specialist team call karega.

Customer: Thank you bhai. Aap samajh rahe ho situation ko. That's all we needed.

Agent: Take care of your father, Arjun. Aur agar koi emergency ho to call karna. Hum yahan hain help ke liye.

Agent: Sir, mujhe samajhna chahiye — aapke paas kya options dekhne mein interest hai? Hum ek partial payment le sakte hain ya phir...

Agent: <interruption> Sir, yeh request bilkul valid hai. Tenure extension aur interest waiver ke liye mujhe yeh escalate karna padega senior management ko. Lekin pehle mujhe ek cheez confirm karna hai — aapka address abhi bhi Sector 12, Gurugram mein hi hai na?

Customer: Haan, woh toh theek hai. Lekin suno, ek aur baat — mujhe abhi ek mahine ka moratorium bhi chahiye. Matlab next EMI 18 February ke baad se shuru ho, isse mujhe thoda breath lene ka time mil jaayega.

Agent: Sir, moratorium aur tenure extension... yeh dono cheezein mujhe escalate karni padegi. Lekin main confirm kar raha hoon — aap restructure ke liye commit hai? Matlab agar hum aapko 6 saal ka tenure de dein aur interest ko bhi adjust kar dein, to aap regularly payment karte rahooge?

Customer: Haan bilkul. Main honest hoon — mera intent default karna nahi hai. Mujhe bass yeh EMI kum chahiye aur ek mahine ka break. Agar tum yeh manage kar do to main aapka sabse loyal customer ban jaaunga.

Agent: Sir, aapki commitment samjh gaya. Main isse immediately senior team ko escalate kar dunga. Unhe 2-3 din lagenge assessment karne mein. Main aapko Thursday ko call karunga — tab tak hume clarity mil jaayegi. Kya Thursday ko 11 AM aapke liye theek hai?

Customer: Haan, Thursday 11 AM theek hai. Lekin Vikram, ek cheez yaad rakna — main genuinely paisa dena chahta hoon. Bas mujhe EMI adjust karna padega warna business hi band ho jaayega.
